verification: All four v7 protocol contracts source-verified on the explorer 2026-09-19 (AssetRegistry, ProtectionOracle, SherwoodVault, ProtectionNote — solc 0.8.35, optimizer 200 runs; constructor args included for the oracle (sequencerUptimeFeed=0, gracePeriod=3600), the vault (MockUSDG, 2000 bps, protocolFeeBps 1000, treasury=deployer) and the note (registry, oracle, vault, maxAssetExposureBps 3000); the registry has none). Same keyless blockscout procedure as v5/v6, with every constructor-args blob byte-validated against its creation transaction first. The v6 lesson applied with a twist: run-latest.json's nonce fields are EMPTY for this broadcast, so a naive sort scrambled the tx-to-name mapping — the byte-check caught it (the 'oracle' tx ended with the note's address: it was setNoteContract) and the mapping was re-derived from on-chain nonces + input tails, correcting six deployTxHashes entries above. Registry and oracle verified in the first wave; vault and note were re-submitted after a network drop (response OK, GUIDs issued, source confirmed via the getsourcecode API).
notes: v7 deployed 2026-09-18: the backer upgrade. SherwoodVault gains a share ledger — anyone can deposit, shares earn 90% of every premium pro rata (protocolFeeBps 1000, hard-capped at 2500, treasury sweeps a bucket that never counts toward backing) and bear payouts pro rata; depositor withdrawals (withdraw by assets, redeem by shares) are capped at availableCapacity, so reserved collateral and the buffer are never withdrawable by anyone — the owner's old withdrawSurplus is gone. ProtectionNote gains the per-stock concentration cap (assetExposure + maxAssetExposureBps, set at deploy to 3000 bps of vault deposits, immutable) on top of the per-holder stack cap. #3 guarantees (expiry, stale rejection, feed binding) were verified as-built, unchanged. 190/190 tests (was 176). Frontend getAsset decode fix shipped with this deploy: the deployed contract returns struct-returns with an outer ABI indirection (pinned by test/ReproGetAsset.t.sol), which had silently emptied every UI asset list. Funding and a v7 demo are the remaining live work; the v6 three-ownership demo never ran and is superseded by this deploy.

v6 deployed 2026-09-16. It carries the six audit fixes on top of everything v5 had: the aggregate exposure cap (one position can no longer back a stack of notes), the 30-day claim window with forfeit semantics (a payout can no longer ride an unbounded horizon past expiry, and the forfeit path reads no price so a dead feed cannot block a release), the per-note settlement feed binding (feed rotation only affects notes created after it), the set-once note-contract binding (repointing — stranding or hostile-wiring — is impossible), and the 18-decimals stock-token validation at registration (live-proven: TSLA registered through it). Commits 828b3b0/8c79c83/1792299/767a2db/15cc107, 176/176 tests. All four contracts explorer-verified (see verification); v6 is unfunded — funding and the demo re-run are the remaining work.

The v5 stack (registry 0x4DE45eCb..., oracle 0x663da2d1..., vault 0x1dd47dE1..., note 0x073AEBD5...) is abandoned with the demo evidence intact: both v4 legs settled 2026-09-14, the three-ownership v5 demo (60/30/0 at one price) settled 2026-09-16 — see the demoNotes (v4) and v5Demo (v5) objects below. The v5Demo evidence was produced by code that predates the six fixes, which is exactly what makes it the correct baseline: the fixes change create/rotation/binding surfaces, not the per-note eligibleAmount payout the demo proves.

v5 deployed 2026-09-14. It carries everything v4 lacked: the Chainlink L2 sequencer-uptime gate (off here by design — 46630 publishes no feed), the 8-decimal feed scale check at registration and rotation, the tightened withdrawSurplus/setBufferBps rules that can never breach invariant 1, and the eligibleAmount settlement basis (payout computed on min(note.amount, stock the owner still holds), reserve always released in full; commit 569ef97, 164/164 tests green). The oracle gained constructor arguments, so this had to be a fresh deploy, not a config nudge.

v4 is abandoned but not deleted: its four contracts stay on-chain with their history, and the demoNotes entries below were executed against the v4 stack (their tx hashes reference v4 addresses 0x70A97604.../0x2725cC6c...). Both v4 demo legs were settled and receipt-verified on 2026-09-14 before the redeploy — payout leg tx 0x79c3366e..., zero-payout leg tx 0x42b9c263... — so the evidence trail lives entirely on one version, which was the point of waiting.

v6 next steps, in order: fund the vault (faucet claim + vault.deposit — the v6 vault holds nothing yet), then run the three-ownership demo against the v6 addresses so the audit fixes carry live evidence. DemoSettle demands DEMO_SETTLE_PRICE explicitly (commit 6340b13) — never rely on a defaulted settlement price.

v4 redeployed for one reason: SherwoodVault.token is immutable, so the v3 vault will forever point at official testnet USDG, a token no protocol wallet has ever received. v3/v2/v1 are abandoned with zero funds and superseded.

Position guard is unchanged in v4 and v5 (create() reverts InsufficientPosition unless the caller holds the protected stock); proven on-chain in the v3 simulation on 2026-09-12 and covered by tests since.

Frontend is repointed at this stack: v4 addresses and MockUSDG are the built-in defaults in frontend/lib/addresses.ts (mirrored in the gitignored frontend/.env.local), and `npm run build` was verified with no env file present, so a Vercel deploy needs no configuration.

Demo write path executed 2026-09-13 on v4: script/DemoCreate.s.sol funded the vault with 50 MockUSDG and bought note 1 (0.1 TSLA, $250 entry, 80%, 1 day) entirely in MockUSDG, paid from the 1,000 claimed from its faucet. Both notes settled 2026-09-14 — see each demoNote's settlement object.

Deploy note for this chain: forge script needs --private-key passed explicitly for --broadcast; relying on the PRIVATE_KEY env var alone left the broadcast using Foundry's default sender and nothing was signed (the first v4 attempt produced zero deployed code). Dry runs need --sender set to the deployer too, or the DemoFeed's onlyOwner check reverts NotOwner. Expect an EIP-3855/PUSH0 warning for chain 46630 — v1 through v5 all deployed and execute fine. On this device run long broadcasts under termux-wake-lock; an unattended v4-era broadcast slept mid-run and submitted nothing.
